fields.title: A merge waits for the validate job
fields.evidence: The `validate` check on the pull request, and the branch rule on `main` in the repository settings.

sections.What it checks:
* [std-CI.the-gate-runs-on-every-pull-request-into-main] says the branch rule on `main` "**MUST** name `validate` as
  the check a merge waits for".
* `eng:std-GATES.a-failing-check-stops-the-change` says branch policy "**MUST** block a merge while any required check
  is failing".
sections.How it works:
`kac.yml` declares a `validate` job whose `needs:` names `corpora`, `tool`, `lint`, `docs`, `round-trip` and
`import-round-trip`. The job itself runs one `echo`. GitHub reports it once every job it needs has passed, so the
branch rule can require that one name.

Three of the jobs it gathers are matrices. `corpora` reports as `corpora (library)` and three more, so a branch rule naming the matrix would wait for a check that never arrives.
sections.Coverage and gaps: The branch rule lives in GitHub's repository settings, and no file in this repository holds it. Nothing in CI reads it, so a rule renamed, relaxed or turned off shows nowhere on the pull request. [ctl-0002] holds the other half of the same promise: whether `validate` still reaches every job.
